skill.name: backend-models
skill.description: Define database models and ORM entities with clear naming, relationships, validation rules, constraints, indexes, and data integrity behavior.
skill.summary: Design consistent database models and ORM entities with strong relationships, validation, and constraints.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

content.value_statement: Database models often drift without clear naming, relationships, and constraints. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through consistent ORM model design.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of model classes and database table definitions.
Supports relationship planning for one-to-many and many-to-many models.
Covers validation rules, database constraints, and foreign keys.
Helps choose model attributes, data types, timestamps, and indexes.
Addresses cascade behavior for related records.
Supports model methods, scopes, and query helper design.
limitations: The detailed standards file is referenced outside the skill package.
It does not inspect a live database schema by itself.
It does not run migrations or verify database constraints.
Framework-specific behavior still needs project context.

use_cases.title: Create a new entity model
use_cases.description: Define fields, relationships, validations, indexes, and timestamps for a new backend domain entity.

use_cases.title: Improve data integrity rules
use_cases.description: Review existing models and identify missing constraints, foreign keys, validations, or cascade behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize ORM patterns
use_cases.description: Align ActiveRecord, SQLAlchemy, Sequelize, or Prisma model changes with shared backend conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a backend model for [entity]. Include fields, data types, required validations, timestamps, and basic indexes.

prompt_templates.title: Add relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the [entity] model to support [relationship]. Include foreign keys, constraints, cascade behavior, and validation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor model structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these existing model requirements and propose a cleaner model structure with stronger naming, constraints, and query helpers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit domain models
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this backend model design for integrity gaps. Check relationships, indexes, validation rules, constraints, scopes, and lifecycle behavior.

output_examples.input: Create a model for customer subscriptions with plans, status, renewal dates, and account ownership.
output_examples.output: A model design with subscription fields, account relationship, status validation, renewal indexes, timestamps, and recommended database constraints.

output_examples.input: Review an order model that stores customer, payment, shipment, and line item information.
output_examples.output: A review that separates relationships, identifies required foreign keys, suggests indexes, and flags missing validations or cascade rules.

output_examples.input: Refactor a product catalog model that mixes pricing, inventory, and category data.
output_examples.output: A normalized model plan with clear entities, relationship boundaries, integrity rules, and query helper recommendations.

best_practices: Provide the target framework and ORM before asking for model changes.
Share existing naming conventions, relationship rules, and migration expectations.
Ask for constraints and indexes with every model design.
anti_patterns: Do not accept model designs without database-level integrity rules.
Do not mix unrelated domain concepts into one oversized model.
Do not use this skill as a substitute for migration testing.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which ORMs does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions ActiveRecord, SQLAlchemy, Sequelize, Prisma, and general ORM model definitions.

faq.question: Can it create migrations?
faq.answer: It can guide model structure, but migration generation depends on project tools and user instructions.

faq.question: Does it verify a live database?
faq.answer: No. It needs project files or user-provided schema details to reason about database state.

faq.question: What should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the entity purpose, fields, relationships, framework, ORM, and data integrity requirements.

faq.question: Is there a security concern?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill references a standards file outside its package, so the author should package that guidance safely.
